newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Drugs companies to press case on prices with EU.
newsitem.headline: Drugs companies to press case on prices with EU.

text.p: The European Union's pharmaceutical sector will urge the EU at a special meeting on Monday in Frankfurt to help it combat trade problems caused by national price controls, industry officials said.

Industry representatives will press their case with EU Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann and Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn, several EU health ministers and other public officials, they said.
Drugs companies complain that cross-border trade is difficult in the EU because the 15 national health systems, which control drugs prices, vary widely.

They are particularly looking for ways to fight the effects of "parallel trade", where importers buy drugs outside of official distribution channels in low-price countries and sell them in high-price ones.

The industry suffered a blow on Thursday when the European Court of Justice ruled against Merck and Co Inc and SmithKline Beecham Plc, saying two British importers must be allowed to import cheap unpatented drugs from Spain and Portugal.

The European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries' Associations (EFPIA) will present a policy agenda on Monday that will include proposals for tackling the question of price differences, industry officials said.

It will propose, for example, that the Commission grant the industry an exemption from EU competition rules to allow companies to control the sales prices of their products within individual countries under some circumstances.
The day-long meeting will also discuss issues such as research, global competitiveness and currency fluctuations, officials said.
